title: Cinematic camera path at constant speed
purpose: Fly a three.js camera through keyframes on a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline at constant speed (an arc-length table), looking at interpolated targets, slerping quaternion keyframes or looking along the direction of travel, with an eased timeline. Use it for fly-throughs, intros, product turntables and replays.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: Pure ES2020, also runs in any browser; applyTo poses a three.js camera through position.set and quaternion.set (cameras look down -Z). Only three.js 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: CameraPath
exports.signature: new CameraPath(keyframes, options = {}); sampleAt(t) -> {position, quaternion, distance, segment, u}; applyTo(camera, t); pointAtDistance(distance); locate(distance) -> {segment, u}; keyframeFractions() -> number[]; length; segments; mode
exports.summary: The path through keyframes {position, target?, quaternion?} with an arc-length table; t in [0, 1] runs the eased timeline at constant speed.

exports.name: catmullRomPoint
exports.signature: catmullRomPoint(p0, p1, p2, p3, u, alpha = 0.5) -> [x, y, z]
exports.summary: A point on the Catmull-Rom segment from p1 to p2 with knot spacing |dp|^alpha.

exports.name: lookRotation
exports.signature: lookRotation(position, target, up = [0, 1, 0]) -> [x, y, z, w]
exports.summary: The orientation of a camera (looking down -Z) at position looking at target.

exports.name: slerpQuaternion
exports.signature: slerpQuaternion(a, b, u) -> [x, y, z, w]
exports.summary: Spherical linear interpolation along the shorter arc.

exports.name: easeTime
exports.summary: Timeline easing: linear, smoothstep or smootherstep, t clamped to [0, 1].

options.name: alpha
options.meaning: Knot spacing exponent: 0 uniform, 0.5 centripetal (no cusps or self-loops in a segment), 1 chordal.

options.name: closed
options.meaning: Join the last keyframe back to the first.

options.name: easing
options.meaning: linear, smoothstep or smootherstep on the timeline.

options.name: up
options.meaning: World up for target and travel orientations.

limits: Constant speed comes from a piecewise-linear arc-length table: speed varies by under 2 percent with 64 samples a segment, not exactly zero. Targets are interpolated with the same spline parameter as positions; quaternion keyframes are slerped per segment, which is continuous but not smooth in angular velocity at keyframes (no squad). The orientation follows look targets with a fixed world up, so a view straight along up uses a stand-in axis and can roll there. No collision, no field-of-view or roll keys. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Centripetal Catmull-Rom spline (Barry and Goldman pyramidal formulation)
Arc-length reparameterization with a cumulative chord table and binary search
Look rotation from an orthonormal basis to a quaternion
Quaternion slerp along the shorter arc
